title: Strumming thin air: why grown-ups fly to Finland to play guitars that do not exist

words.note: 吉他、尤克里里的弹法：strum a guitar。也可以说手指无聊地敲：strum on the table。
words.ctx: Strumming thin air: why grown-ups fly to Finland to play guitars that do not exist

ex.en: He sat on the steps, [[strumming]] an old guitar.
ex.zh: 他坐在台阶上，拨着一把旧吉他。

ex.en: She [[strummed]] a few chords and began to sing.
ex.zh: 她扫了几个和弦，开始唱歌。

words.note: 城市、国家、机构举办活动：host the Olympics。名词 host 是主人、主持人。

words.note: as if 后面用过去时或过去完成时，表示“其实并不是这样”：He talks as if he knew everything.（他说话好像什么都知道，其实不然）。说过去的事用 had done。

ex.en: She looked at me [[as if]] I had said something rude.

words.conn: 主句 + as if + 主语 + 过去时 / 过去完成时（与事实相反）

pick.q: He talked about Paris as if he ___ there many times, but he never had.
pick.why: 其实他没去过，是和过去事实相反的想象，as if 后用过去完成时 had been。

pick.q: She was so calm, ___ nothing had happened.
pick.why: “好像什么都没发生”用 as if；even if 是“即使”，意思不对。

words.zh: 固定节目、常设活动；固定装置

words.ctx: What began as a joke at a local music festival has grown into an international fixture, with national champions from dozens of countries competing for the title.

ex.en: The Christmas market is a [[fixture]] of the city's winter.
ex.zh: 圣诞市集是这座城市冬天的固定节目。

ex.en: The old man became a [[fixture]] in the park.

words.expr: nor + 助动词 + 主语（倒装）
words.note: 前面已经是否定句，接着说“也不……”，用 nor，后面要倒装：助动词 / be / 情态动词放到主语前。I can't swim, nor can my brother.（我不会游泳，我弟弟也不会）。口语里常用 neither 代替。
words.ctx: Contestants may not touch a real instrument, nor may they rely on backing musicians; the guitar must be entirely imaginary.

ex.en: I don't like coffee, [[nor]] does my sister.
ex.zh: 我不喜欢咖啡，我姐姐也不喜欢。

ex.en: He never called, [[nor]] did he write.
ex.zh: 他从没打过电话，也没写过信。

words.conn: 否定句, nor + 助动词 / be / 情态动词 + 主语 + ...

pick.q: She didn't come to the party, nor ___ a message.
pick.why: nor 开头要倒装，助动词 did 放到主语 she 前：nor did she send。

pick.q: I can't drive, ___ can my husband.
pick.why: 前面是否定，“也不会”用 nor；so can my husband 是“他也会”，用在肯定句后。

words.zh: 捕捉、抓住（精髓、注意力）；俘获
words.note: capture the spirit / mood（抓住精神 / 氛围），capture attention（吸引注意）。也指拍下画面：capture a moment。
words.ctx: Nobody pretends this is a serious peace plan, but the slogan captures the spirit of the thing: harmless, generous and slightly absurd.

ex.en: The photo [[captures]] the joy of the moment.
ex.zh: 这张照片捕捉到了那一刻的喜悦。

ex.en: The song [[captured]] the mood of the summer.
ex.zh: 这首歌唱出了那个夏天的氛围。

words.note: harm（伤害）+ -less（没有）。a harmless joke（无伤大雅的玩笑）。反义 harmful。
words.ctx: Nobody pretends this is a serious peace plan, but the slogan captures the spirit of the thing: harmless, generous and slightly absurd.

ex.en: Most spiders are [[harmless]].
ex.zh: 大多数蜘蛛是无害的。

ex.en: It was just a [[harmless]] joke.
ex.zh: 那只是个无伤大雅的玩笑。

words.note: 比 silly 更强，常带“不合常理”的意思。名词 absurdity。
words.ctx: Nobody pretends this is a serious peace plan, but the slogan captures the spirit of the thing: harmless, generous and slightly absurd.

ex.en: It's [[absurd]] to pay that much for a sandwich.
ex.zh: 一个三明治卖那么贵，太离谱了。

ex.en: The idea sounded [[absurd]] at first.
ex.zh: 这个主意一开始听起来很荒唐。

words.zh: 令人耳目一新的；提神的
words.note: refreshing honesty（难得的坦诚），a refreshing drink（清爽的饮料）。
words.ctx: There is something refreshing about a contest in which no one can be accused of having an unfair advantage.

ex.en: It's [[refreshing]] to meet someone so honest.
ex.zh: 遇到这么坦诚的人，真让人耳目一新。

ex.en: A cold glass of lemonade is very [[refreshing]].
ex.zh: 一杯冰柠檬水很解渴提神。

cloze.before: There is something
cloze.after: about a contest in which no one can be accused of having an unfair advantage.
cloze.szh: 一场谁也不会被指责占了不公平优势的比赛，自有一种让人耳目一新的地方。

words.note: accuse sb of (doing) sth：指责某人……。注意介词用 of，不是 for。名词 accusation。
words.ctx: There is something refreshing about a contest in which no one can be accused of having an unfair advantage.

ex.en: He was [[accused of]] cheating in the exam.
ex.zh: 他被指控考试作弊。

ex.en: The company was [[accused of]] hiding the truth.
ex.zh: 这家公司被指责隐瞒真相。

cloze.before: There is something refreshing about a contest in which no one can be
cloze.after: of having an unfair advantage.
cloze.szh: 一场谁也不会被指责占了不公平优势的比赛，自有一种让人耳目一新的地方。

words.note: have / gain / give sb an unfair advantage。have an advantage over sb：比某人有优势。
words.ctx: There is something refreshing about a contest in which no one can be accused of having an unfair advantage.

ex.en: Using a calculator would give you an [[unfair advantage]].
ex.zh: 用计算器会让你占不公平的便宜。

ex.en: Rich families can buy their children an [[unfair advantage]].
ex.zh: 有钱人家能给孩子买来不公平的优势。

cloze.before: There is something refreshing about a contest in which no one can be accused of having an
cloze.after: advantage.
cloze.szh: 一场谁也不会被指责占了不公平优势的比赛，自有一种让人耳目一新的地方。

words.note: have the nerve to do：有胆量做（也可以是“竟敢”）。lose one's nerve：临阵退缩。get on sb's nerves：让人心烦。
words.ctx: No expensive equipment is needed, and a child with enough nerve can, in principle, beat a professional musician.

ex.en: I didn't have the [[nerve]] to ask her out.
ex.zh: 我没胆量约她出去。

ex.en: Loud music gets on my [[nerves]].
ex.zh: 吵闹的音乐让我心烦。

cloze.before: No expensive equipment is needed, and a child with enough
cloze.after: can, in principle, beat a professional musician.
cloze.szh: 不需要昂贵的设备，一个胆子够大的孩子，理论上也能打败专业音乐人。

words.note: 常和 in practice（实际上，之前学过）对比：In principle it's easy; in practice it's hard.
words.ctx: No expensive equipment is needed, and a child with enough nerve can, in principle, beat a professional musician.

ex.en: [[In principle]], anyone can apply.
ex.zh: 原则上谁都可以申请。

ex.en: We agree [[in principle]], but the details need work.
ex.zh: 我们原则上同意，但细节还需要再谈。

cloze.before: No expensive equipment is needed, and a child with enough nerve can, in
cloze.after: , beat a professional musician.
cloze.szh: 不需要昂贵的设备，一个胆子够大的孩子，理论上也能打败专业音乐人。

words.note: 也说 in an era when / at a time when。when 引导定语从句，后面接完整句子。
words.ctx: In an age when so much of life is measured, ranked and sold, a world title for doing nothing at all is a small act of rebellion.

ex.en: [[In an age when]] everyone has a phone, few people wear watches.
ex.zh: 在人人都有手机的时代，很少有人戴手表。

ex.en: [[In an age when]] news travels fast, rumours spread faster.
ex.zh: 在消息传得飞快的时代，谣言传得更快。

cloze.before: In an
cloze.after: when so much of life is measured, ranked and sold, a world title for doing nothing at all is a small act of rebellion.
cloze.szh: 在一个生活里太多东西都要被衡量、排名、拿来卖钱的时代，一项“什么都不做”的世界冠军，算是一种小小的反叛。

words.note: 动词 rebel（反抗），形容词 rebellious（叛逆的）：a rebellious teenager。
words.ctx: In an age when so much of life is measured, ranked and sold, a world title for doing nothing at all is a small act of rebellion.

ex.en: Dyeing her hair green was her small [[rebellion]].
ex.zh: 把头发染成绿色是她的小小叛逆。

ex.en: The king crushed the [[rebellion]].
ex.zh: 国王镇压了起义。

cloze.szh: 在一个生活里太多东西都要被衡量、排名、拿来卖钱的时代，一项“什么都不做”的世界冠军，算是一种小小的反叛。

words.note: 肌肉酸痛、喉咙痛常用 sore：a sore throat, sore legs。sore point：痛处、敏感话题。
words.ctx: And unlike most championships, this one leaves its fans with nothing worse than a sore throat.

ex.en: My legs are [[sore]] after yesterday's run.
ex.zh: 昨天跑完步腿好酸。

ex.en: I've got a [[sore]] throat, so I'll stay home.
ex.zh: 我嗓子疼，就待在家吧。

cloze.before: And unlike most championships, this one leaves its fans with nothing worse than a
cloze.after: throat.
cloze.szh: 而且和大多数锦标赛不同，这一场留给粉丝的，最糟也不过是喊哑了的嗓子。

words.note: 也说 judging from。Judging by his face, the news was bad.（看他的脸色，消息不好）。
words.ctx: The guitars may be imaginary; the joy, judging by the crowds, is anything but.

ex.en: [[Judging by]] the queue, the food must be good.
ex.zh: 看这排队的阵势，菜一定好吃。

ex.en: [[Judging by]] her smile, she passed the test.
ex.zh: 看她笑得这么开心，应该是考过了。

cloze.after: by the crowds, is anything but.
cloze.szh: 吉他也许是想象出来的；可从观众的热情来看，那份快乐绝不是假的。

words.note: anything but + 形容词 = 一点也不：The hotel was anything but cheap.（那家酒店一点也不便宜）。注意和 nothing but（只是）意思相反。
words.ctx: The guitars may be imaginary; the joy, judging by the crowds, is anything but.

ex.en: The exam was [[anything but]] easy.
ex.zh: 这次考试一点也不简单。

ex.en: He looked [[anything but]] happy.
ex.zh: 他看起来一点也不开心。
